correctness.rationale: For every direction the four facet inequalities give the two radial endpoints; signed permutations preserve full chord length and give 48 equal-area chambers. In a chamber with x≥y≥z≥0 the two denominators are x+y±z, so in the stated angular coordinates L=2A√(1+q²)/(A²−q²). This increases for q>0, and the factored polynomial in the proof bounds the maximum at the upper chamber corner. The lower corner gives the stated minimum; continuity on S² gives the full interval as support. Solving the quadratic in q² and rationalizing matches q_* with the angular cap, and integrating the area element gives 12/π with no positive-area equality levels. The minimum chart works across the adjacent sign/order chambers: its even quadratic form has coefficients 1/√2 and √2, hence area π per unit deficit. At the maximum the nonnegative homogeneous leading deficit is −6 min(a,b,c) on the tangent plane, positive off the origin and comparable to the Euclidean norm; its unit sublevel is the triangle of side 1/√2 and area √3/8. For each extremum, the rescaled sets lie in a fixed compact disk, their indicators converge off null boundaries, and the smooth area Jacobians converge uniformly to one; normalized densities converge in L¹. The symmetry-equivalent oriented marks carry equal weights. Multiplicities 12 and 8 divided by 4π yield the two stated asymptotic constants, not exact finite-deficit identities. The frozen NumPy/SciPy check.py and recorded diagnostics were inspected, not executed; they do not establish the continuum limits.
